correctness.rationale: Using four-point δ4=(1/2)sup of the largest-minus-second-largest among three distance-pair sums, a 0-hyperbolic tree factor T makes the top two sums of a_ij equal A. For max(a_ij,b_ij) with diam(Y)<=D: if A>D, every c pairing sum ≤A+D and at least two are ≥A; hence defect≤D. If A≤D, all c pair distances≤D, and metric triangle inequalities yield S_max≤S_mid+S_min and S_max≤2D, hence defect≤D. Thus δ4(T×∞Y)≤D/2. Aggregate k-1 factors into Y of diameter D2. For lower bound, any two factors of diam≥L contain isometric geodesic length-L segments, yielding an ℓ∞ square with compass points and pair sums (2L,L,L), so δ4≥L/2 for every L<D2. Supremum gives D2/2 even for nonattained diameters or D2 infinite. Singleton factors contribute zero. Independent exact grid quartets confirm representative 2/3-factor cases but are not the proof.
